I would love to help you with that! This is about finding equivalent fractions. 

Look at the denominators, which are the bottom numbers. How do we get from 3 to 6 by multiplying?
is it 4/6 because you multiply the bottom by 2 so you have to multiply the top by 2 as well Next one: 2/9 + 4/9?

Spot on with the first one, well done! 

Now, for 2/9 + 4/9, notice that both fractions already have the exact same denominator. When adding fractions like this, what do you do with the numerators on the top?
it is 6/9 because you just add the top numbers together and keep the bottom number the same Next one: 1/4 + 1/8?

You nailed that explanation, excellent work! 

For 1/4 + 1/8, the denominators are different, so we can't add them straight away. Can you think of how we can make the denominators the same by changing 1/4 into an equivalent fraction with an 8 on the bottom?
